content.user_title: Build Modern React and Next.js Interfaces
content.value_statement: Modern frontend work often requires fast, accessible, and maintainable interfaces across devices. This skill guides React and Next.js implementation with practical architecture choices.
actual_capabilities: Builds React and Next.js component plans using React 19 and App Router patterns.
Recommends responsive layouts with Tailwind CSS, CSS Modules, CSS Grid, and Flexbox.
Guides client state and server state choices across common React libraries.
Addresses accessibility with WCAG, ARIA, keyboard navigation, and form validation.
Reviews performance concerns such as Core Web Vitals, image loading, and code splitting.
Suggests frontend testing with React Testing Library, Jest, Playwright, Cypress, Storybook, and axe-core.
limitations: Does not replace running tests, browser checks, or production monitoring.
Does not provide backend architecture except where it connects to frontend behavior.
Requires project context to choose exact libraries, file paths, and deployment settings.
May reference newer framework features that need version checks.

use_cases.title: Deliver a React Feature
use_cases.description: Plan component structure, state ownership, loading states, errors, and responsive behavior for a product feature.

use_cases.title: Improve Accessibility Quality
use_cases.description: Review UI flows for WCAG concerns, ARIA patterns, keyboard navigation, focus management, and test coverage.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Product Page
use_cases.description: Turn requirements into a Next.js page plan with data fetching, layout choices, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component for state, accessibility, responsive layout, and performance. Explain the recommended changes before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Responsive Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a responsive Next.js page plan for this feature. Include component boundaries, loading states, error states, and accessibility checks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose State and Data Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the state and data fetching approach for this workflow. Compare local state, server state, caching, optimistic updates, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Frontend Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this React and Next.js architecture. Recommend routing, rendering, testing, performance, accessibility, and design system improvements.

output_examples.input: Optimize a dashboard page that feels slow on mobile.
output: A prioritized performance diagnosis covering rendering, images, bundle size, and data loading.
A set of changes to improve Core Web Vitals and reduce layout shifts.
Validation steps for Lighthouse, browser profiling, and real device checks.

output_examples.input: Create an accessible data table with sorting and filtering.
output: A component plan with keyboard support, semantic markup, focus behavior, and empty states.
Testing guidance for screen readers, axe-core, responsive layouts, and interaction states.

output_examples.input: Modernize a form with optimistic updates.
output: A workflow design for validation, pending state, optimistic UI, rollback, and error recovery.
Recommendations for React actions, server mutations, and user feedback patterns.

best_practices: Provide framework versions, routing mode, styling stack, and browser support.
Define acceptance criteria for accessibility, loading states, errors, and responsive behavior.
Run linting, tests, Lighthouse, and real device checks after implementation.
anti_patterns: Requesting broad redesigns without target users, content, or devices.
Shipping generated UI without keyboard, screen reader, and contrast checks.
Mixing many state libraries in one feature without a clear ownership model.

faq.question: What projects is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for React, Next.js, and TypeScript frontend work that needs implementation guidance.

faq.question: Can it write production code?
faq.answer: It can produce implementation plans and code guidance, but you must test changes in your project.

faq.question: Does it handle accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes WCAG, ARIA, keyboard navigation, focus management, and accessible form patterns.

faq.question: Does it support performance work?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Core Web Vitals, bundle analysis, lazy loading, code splitting, and rendering optimization.

faq.question: Can it choose a state management library?
faq.answer: It can compare React state, context, Zustand, Jotai, Redux Toolkit, React Query, and SWR for your requirements.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide framework versions, page goals, current code, target devices, styling tools, data needs, and test expectations.
